links.outcome: LLM structured-extraction content errors against human consensus reference, comparing single LLMs to multi-LLM consensus
links.effect: Consensus reduced errors ~30% versus best single LLM to 6.7% (36 errors, 93.30% accuracy); true-error rate 1.48% vs neurologists ~2% (p=0.6447).
links.quote: Using this method, we were able to decrease the error rate by around another 30% compared to the best performing LLM.

links.outcome: LLM consensus extraction accuracy compared with neurology specialists and trained medical personnel on same reports
links.effect: LLM consensus true-error rate 1.48% vs NSP ~2%; difference not significant (p=0.6447; OR 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).
links.quote: The difference between the LLM consensus evaluation and the NSPs was not significant ( p = 0.6447; odds ratio = 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).

links.outcome: Structural and data-format errors across prompt designs and structured output functions
links.effect: Structured output function reduced column errors from 30/18/113 to 0/0/0; data-format errors reduced up to 88%, though not fully error-free.
links.quote: By using these methods, we were able to reduce the rate of incorrect data formats by up to 88 percent ( Table 2 ).
